newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina says 1996 fiscal deficit $5.89 billion.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says 1996 fiscal deficit $5.89 billion.

text.p: Argentina's Economy Ministry said Wednesday the country's 1996 fiscal deficit without privatization income was $5.89 billion.
The deficit in the final quarter of the year was $1.84 billion.

The 1996 shortfall was just shy of the $6.0 billion agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF). That deficit should be cut to $3.0 billion in 1997 or $4.5 billion when taking into account the transfer of provincial pensions to the central state.
The 1996 deficit compares with a fiscal gap of $2.54 billion in 1995, although the 1995 figure has been challenged by the IMF, which estimates it was around $1.0 billion larger.
Total current revenues were $46.0 billion and total expenditures $48.46 billion, resulting in a $2.46 billion deficit.
Total 1996 capital expenditures were $3.56 billion, mostly due to the transfer of a larger chunk of federal tax revenues to provinces under the so-called "Coparticipation law".
